items.title: [apnews.com] European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027. The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind. Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Researchers used miniature solar-powered transmitters to track a male Rufous hummingbird from Alabama to Alaska, recording a 4,055-mile journey in 38 days—the longest hummingbird migration documented to date. They tagged the bird in Lillian, Alabama, on March 27, 2025, and it reached Juneau on May 3. The team fitted 11 hummingbirds with the devices in coastal Alabama and Florida in spring 2025 to track their movements across North America. The study authors said Rufous and ruby-throated hummingbird populations have recently declined; further research is needed to assess any long-term effects of wearing the transmitters.

items.title: [physicsworld.com] Scientists propose supercritical fluids drove deep Mariana volcanic eruptions
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Researchers propose that supercritical water in magma could explain how volcanic deposits formed more than 6,000 meters down the Mariana Trench wall, building on the discovery of unusually deep pyroclastic rocks. At those pressures, water behaves neither like an ordinary liquid nor a gas and expands far less than steam. The team says this may have enabled magma to fragment without the force of a land eruption. The mechanism remains uncertain: researchers have not found the vents or directly observed an eruption. Rock samples contain “double breccia,” suggesting two closely spaced episodes of fracturing — one possibly linked to supercritical fluid and another to its conversion to steam at the seafloor. The team plans further analysis of the volcanic material and aims to explore farther along the plate boundary. Jason/Medea cannot descend below 6,500 meters, short of the Challenger Deep floor at about 11,000 meters.

A study published in *Nature Astronomy* suggests that a stretch of the Milky Way’s Norma arm traced by masers may instead be a star-forming shock front along the leading edge of the galaxy’s central bar. The University of Sydney-led team reached that interpretation by comparing galaxy simulations with existing maser measurements; it did not directly image the shock front or collect new observations. The researchers say the result concerns only the maser segment near the bar’s end, not the entire Norma-Outer arm, and requires further investigation.

items.title: [livescience.com] Four Guangxi fossil teeth point to Denisovans and another ancient lineage
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Researchers analyzing four fossil teeth from two caves in China’s Guangxi region identified Denisovan-related remains and evidence of a potentially distinct ancient human lineage, according to a study published in Nature on Nov. 25. The two Longchuandong teeth align with Denisovans, while two teeth from Chuanshandong—at least 100,800 years old—have traits that do not readily match any known East Asian Homo group. The findings suggest different archaic human populations lived in southern China during overlapping periods, but researchers cannot yet confidently assign the Chuanshandong teeth to a named group. Warm, humid conditions in the region hinder ancient DNA preservation, so researchers analyzed tooth shape and proteins. They say more fossils and molecular evidence are needed to establish the teeth’s evolutionary relationships.

items.title: [medicalxpress.com] Scandinavian study finds no increased developmental risk from prenatal ADHD drugs
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

A study of more than 3.6 million children born in Denmark, Norway and Sweden found no increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders associated with mothers’ use of ADHD medication during pregnancy. Researchers tracked the children for about a decade; 7,595 had prenatal exposure, including 2,389 exposed in the second or third trimester. The researchers said the findings do not support stopping medication solely over concerns about children’s future neurodevelopment, but stressed that treatment decisions should be made individually with a health professional. The study was observational. The authors said unmeasured factors, such as maternal ADHD severity and genetics, and the relatively small exposed group limit conclusions about some specific conditions.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope identified a quasar candidate in its wide-area survey data, beyond the distance the mission was designed to map; ground- and space-based observatories then confirmed it. European Southern Observatory astronomer Julien Wolf led the discovery. The object, J1504+6252, was seen as it existed about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Follow-up observations with the James Webb and Hubble space telescopes, among other observatories, established its record distance. Euclid launched in 2023 to survey galaxies and help investigate dark matter and dark energy; the team published its findings in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming. By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago, signaling the possible start of a new glacial period. But by the 1960s, rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Oregon State University researchers grew potatoes through their full life cycle in simulated lunar regolith after adding organic matter; a mixture containing 30% vermicompost produced yields comparable to those in terrestrial soil. The NASA-funded experiment took place in a greenhouse on Earth and used simulated material, not material collected on the moon, so it does not establish that crops can be grown on the lunar surface. The trial used five regolith simulants and the Modoc potato variety. Researchers plan to test 10 more potato varieties and are studying growth in larger pots; the first trial’s small pots produced small tubers.

items.title: [medicalxpress.com] Study links very large and small waists to higher death risk
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

A study of more than 17 million South Korean adults found that both unusually large and unusually small waist measurements were associated with a higher risk of death across weight and age groups. The lowest observed risk was associated with waist circumferences of 80–94 centimeters in men and 75–89 centimeters in women. The association between waist circumference and death risk was stronger at older ages, especially among women 75 and older. Researchers analyzed routine health-check measurements from 2009–10 and tracked survival for nearly 14 years, through June 30, 2024. The study was observational and cannot show that waist size causes death. Among people with normal weight or overweight whose waist circumference was high for their body mass index (BMI), reducing waist circumference without necessarily losing weight appeared to offer a greater survival benefit than losing weight while reducing waist circumference, the authors said.

items.title: [phys.org] Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science. The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters.

items.title: [latimes.com] California king tides flood coastal homes as warming raises water levels
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Unusually warm Pacific waters and a strong El Niño raised coastal water levels as November king tides flooded California homes and streets, damaged seawalls and contributed to the collapse of part of Pacifica’s pier. Los Angeles, Santa Barbara and La Jolla set or matched tide records, while floodwaters in Pacifica overwhelmed pumps despite sandbags and other preparations. Ocean warming expands seawater, while human-caused sea-level rise raises the starting point for each tide. items.title: [frontpageafricaonline.com] COP31 draft proposes $120 billion in annual adaptation finance by 2035
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

A draft COP31 agreement proposes at least $120 billion a year in adaptation finance for developing countries by 2035, alongside accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels. Released by the conference presidency on Nov. 16, the text remains under negotiation and does not represent an agreed position; the talks in Antalya, Türkiye, are scheduled to end Nov. 20. African negotiators are pressing for predictable grants, measurable delivery milestones and finance that does not deepen debt. The United Nations Environment Programme estimates developing countries will need $305 billion annually for adaptation by 2035, while international public adaptation finance reached $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in 2024. Ghanaian Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings also called for funding to restore land and rivers damaged by mining and for greater local processing of Africa’s minerals.

Developer Cody Collier has released NO SPEAKER, a free, open-source tool that makes a MacBook’s Force Touch trackpad produce speech, tones and simple music through its haptic motor, even with the laptop’s speakers muted. items.title: [english.aawsat.com] Israel strikes alleged Hezbollah arms shipment near Syria-Lebanon border
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Israel struck a mountainous area near Janta in eastern Lebanon on Monday, Nov. 16, saying it targeted a weapons shipment sent from Syria for Hezbollah. Lebanon’s National News Agency reported that the strike hit the Al-Shaara area at dawn and caused no casualties or damage. The Israeli military also said it detained two men in southern Lebanon whom it described as Hezbollah-guided operatives; Lebanese state media said Israeli forces seized two brothers in Shebaa. A U.S.-backed framework for Lebanon calls for Hezbollah’s disarmament, an Israeli troop withdrawal and Lebanese army deployment in the south, but implementation has stalled and Hezbollah has rejected surrendering its weapons. Haaretz described the attack as a departure from Israel’s prolonged restraint on strikes deep inside Lebanon. Israeli forces continue operating in a self-declared security zone along the border.
